MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "osteosarcoma"
- "AP (anteroposterior) and lateral X-ray of the distal femur, physis open: a **metaphyseal, central, mixed** lesion, **ill-defined**, with cortical destruction."
- "Sunburst and **Codman's triangle**, soft-tissue mass with **tumour bone**. So → **malignant**; in a teenager → **osteosarcoma** until proved otherwise; differential Ewing, osteomyelitis."
- "Next → MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) of the **whole bone** (skip lesions), chest CT (computed tomography), bone scan, then **core biopsy** at the treating centre."
- "Treatment → neoadjuvant **MAP** chemotherapy → **wide resection**, mostly limb salvage → adjuvant chemotherapy; **>90% necrosis** = good response; localised survival ≈70%."

HIGH YIELD — Memory line
- **10–20 years · knee metaphysis · sunburst + Codman + tumour bone · malignant osteoid · MAP chemo + wide resection**

### 1 Definition
- **Malignant**, bony origin: **malignant cells make osteoid** — any osteoid-making sarcoma, even in soft tissue · conventional = primary **intramedullary high-grade**, the commonest type (Greenspan; OKU Tumors 4)

### 2 Origin
- Tissue → bony origin (Lichtenstein–Dahlin) → → 1 Introduction · **primary** (de novo) or **secondary** (Paget, radiation) → → Subtypes
- Peak at the time and sites of **fastest bone growth** · Prof Abosena's risk factors → rapid growth, radiation, Paget, genetic syndromes

| Genetics | Fact |
|---|---|
| **Rb** (13q14) | Mutated in ≈35% (Miller); hereditary retinoblastoma → osteosarcoma is its commonest second cancer |
| **p53** (17p13) | Altered in most; **Li-Fraumeni** = germline p53 |
| Other syndromes | Rothmund-Thomson (RECQL4), Werner, Bloom |

### 3 Incidence
- **Age** → **Bimodal**: 2nd decade, then 7th–8th decades (mostly secondary) · **Sex** → slight **male** predominance · **Relative incidence** → commonest **primary non-haematological** malignant bone tumour, ≈20% of primary bone malignancies (OKU Tumors 4; Campbell) → → 1 Rank line

### 4 Sites
- **Longitudinal** → **Metaphysis** (≈10% diaphyseal, <1% epiphyseal), crosses the physis · **Transverse** → **central**, intramedullary · **Special sites** → any bone, hand rare · **distal femur + proximal tibia ≈50%**, then **proximal humerus** (Campbell; OKU Tumors 4)
- Proximal tibia, film and bone scan, 13-year-old (Greenspan)

### 5 Clinical presentation
- **Local** → **Pain** and swelling; may ease with rest; night pain in only ≈25% (OKU Tumors 4)
CLINICAL PEARL — the missed X-ray
- Median delay ≈4 months, pain blamed on growth or sport · commonest error = **no X-ray** or not repeating it (OKU Tumors 4; Campbell)

- **Systemic** → uncommon; **Complications** → spine → neurological deficit · pelvis → bowel symptoms

- Metastases at diagnosis → visible **20–25%**, micrometastases **80–90%** (why everyone gets chemotherapy); **lung ≈80%**, then bone (OKU Tumors 4; Miller)

### 7 Labs
- **Routine** → **ALP (alkaline phosphatase)** and **LDH (lactate dehydrogenase)** → raised in many; high values = **worse prognosis**; prognostic, not diagnostic (OKU Tumors 4)
- **Specific** → No tumour marker; before chemotherapy → routine labs, audiometry, echocardiography (Prof Abosena)

### 8 Biopsy
- **Modality** → **Core needle biopsy** (image-guided) → standard; open biopsy if needle fails or by the definitive surgeon → → 2 Biopsy

CLINICAL PEARL — the biopsy track
- **Open biopsy rules** → Biopsy at the treating centre, longitudinal, one compartment; the track is excised with the tumour

**Pathology**
- Hard, white, fleshy mass, ossified and soft parts, haemorrhage · frankly malignant spindle cells **making osteoid**

- Gross specimen, distal femur (Greenspan)
- Histology: malignant spindle cells making osteoid (Campbell)
- Histology: malignant osteoid (Prof Abosena)

- Types → **osteoblastic ≈50%** · chondroblastic ≈25% · fibroblastic ≈25% · malignant osteoid = lace-like, not rimmed by normal osteoblasts (Greenspan; Prof Abosena)

### 9 Differential diagnosis
- **Location groups** → **By location** → teenage metaphysis: osteosarcoma, Ewing → → 1 Differential · **by film** → bone-forming: **osteomyelitis**, aggressive osteoblastoma
- **Histology groups** → **By cell** → small cell osteosarcoma vs Ewing, lymphoma; fibroblastic osteosarcoma vs fibrosarcoma
- **Special DD** → **Mimics** → osteomyelitis · subtypes → ABC (aneurysmal bone cyst) for telangiectatic; osteochondroma, myositis ossificans for parosteal

| Film | Tumour bone, sunburst, Codman | Permeative, onion skin, big soft-tissue mass | Destruction, sequestrum, fat planes blurred |

9.01.10.b:
- **Enneking** → **High grade** (Broders 3–4; >90% of intramedullary tumours) · Enneking → mostly **IIB**, high grade, extracompartmental (Miller)
- **AJCC** → IA/IB low grade ≤8 / >8 cm · IIA/IIB high grade · **III skip lesion** · IVA lung · IVB other metastases · weight → metastases > skip > grade > size (Campbell; Miller)

9.01.11.b:
- **Margin** → **Wide** margin (marginal → recurrence 25–50%, intralesional ≈100%) · **Malignant local** → **limb salvage** in ≈85–90%, survival = amputation; amputate only if a functional, disease-free limb is impossible (Miller; OKU Tumors 4) → → 3 Limb salvage

- Reconstruction → endoprosthesis (commonest; expandable in children) · biological: fibula, allograft, recycled (frozen) bone, condyle-sparing · **rotationplasty**: the ankle works as a knee in a growing child

- Proximal tibia: film, resection, endoprosthesis, specimen (Durfee 2016)
- Femur, 8-year-old: resection and expandable prosthesis (Greenspan)

- Expandable proximal tibial spacer (Greenspan) | distal femoral endoprosthesis (Prof Abosena)
- Condyle-sparing resection | rotationplasty (Prof Abosena)

- **Systemic** → Localised → **neoadjuvant chemotherapy → wide resection → adjuvant chemotherapy**; metastatic → the same + resection of all lung metastases

| Chemotherapy (OKU Tumors 4) | Fact |
| --- | --- |
| **MAP** | High-dose **M**ethotrexate, **A**driamycin (doxorubicin), **P**latinum (cisplatin) |
| Schedule | ≈10 weeks (2 cycles) → surgery → restart within 3 weeks → ≈20 weeks more |
| Why neoadjuvant | Treats micrometastases at once · time to plan the implant · measures **necrosis** |
| Poor responders | Adding ifosfamide/etoposide (MAPIE) → no gain, more toxicity |
| Toxicities | → → 3 Treatment principles |
- **Huvos necrosis grades** of the resected tumour (Sadikovic 2010; Moukengue 2022):

| Huvos grade | Necrosis | Response |
|---|---|---|
| I | <50% (little or no effect) | Poor |
| II | 50–89% | Poor |
| III | **≥90%**, viable foci | **Good** |
| IV | 100%, no viable tumour | **Good** |

- **>90% necrosis** = good response, better survival; changing drugs for poor responders has **not** helped → necrosis reflects biology (OKU Tumors 4)
- After chemotherapy → reactive sclerotic rim, narrow zone; do not read it as benign (Greenspan)

- CT before and after chemotherapy (Greenspan)
- Tibia after 3 months of chemotherapy: sclerotic rim (Greenspan)

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| metaphyseal | central | mixed | well-defined (sclerotic rim) | thinning | none | **malignant** |

- Proximal tibia, 15-year-old: film and angiogram before and after chemotherapy (Greenspan)

- Complete tumour necrosis after chemotherapy, histology (Campbell)

CLINICAL PEARL — necrosis, not size
- Read on the **specimen**, not by shrinkage (osteosarcoma shrinks less); good responders 8-year **87%** vs poor **52%** (OKU Tumors 4; Provisor 1997)

- **Radiotherapy** → osteosarcoma is radioresistant; only unresectable tumour, positive margin, palliation (OKU Tumors 4)

CLINICAL PEARL — lung metastases are not the end
- Resect all lung metastases: few nodules, late (>24 months) → best; >8 nodules, >3 cm, early → poor (OKU Tumors 4; Campbell)

PITFALL — fixing the fracture
- Prof Abosena → splint, chemotherapy, **never** fix before diagnosis (the track spreads tumour) · books → no automatic amputation; limb salvage if local control is possible; fracture worsens survival (OKU Tumors 4)
- Say → "splint, biopsy, chemotherapy, then wide resection; amputation only if a margin is impossible"

9.01.12.b:
- **Prognosis** → **Prognostic factors** (real question) → **metastasis** first, then necrosis <90%, axial or proximal site, large size, high ALP/LDH, inadequate margin, pathological fracture (Campbell; OKU Tumors 4; Miller)

| Outcome | Number (OKU Tumors 4; Campbell) |
| --- | --- |
| **Localised**, chemo + wide surgery | ≈**70%** 5-year (60–75%) |

- **Prognostic factors?** → metastasis (most powerful), necrosis <90%, axial site, size, ALP/LDH, margin
- **Huvos grades?** → I <50% · II 50–89% · III ≥90% · IV 100% necrosis; III–IV = good

PITFALL — telangiectatic: worse or better?
- Then → thought more aggressive with a worse outcome, "once considered a lethal" tumour (OKU Tumors 4; Bacci 2001) · Greenspan → "very aggressive" · Prof Abosena → unfavourable
- Now → neoadjuvant chemotherapy: good necrosis **96% vs 68%**, disease-free **83% vs 55%** against conventional (Bacci 2001); survival equal (Weiss 2007)
- Why → "aggressive" = **local** behaviour (lytic, destructive, fracture 31–43%); survival follows **chemotherapy response**, and it is very chemosensitive (Weiss 2007; Angelini 2016)
- Say → "locally aggressive, fractures often, but very chemosensitive → prognosis **equal to or better** than conventional"

MUST-KNOW — criteria of radiation-induced sarcoma (Cahan 1948; all four; same wording as 3 Treatment)
- 1) **Irradiated site** → previous radiotherapy there, usually ≥3,000 rads within 4 weeks; reported after only 800 rads (Greenspan; OKU Tumors 4)
- 2) **Inside the field** → the sarcoma arises within the radiation field (OKU Tumors 4; Greenspan)
- 3) **Latent period ≥3 years** → average 11 years, range 4–40 (Greenspan; OKU Tumors 4)
- 4) **Different histology** → not the same type as the original (benign or malignant) lesion that was irradiated (OKU Tumors 4; Greenspan)
